notes: B, C and O are fixed material points on one rigid BCO wheel-carrier link; their pairwise distances BC, BO and CO are invariant for every mechanism pose.
H is an auxiliary construction point fixed in the same BCO body frame; H, B and C are collinear in the order H-B-C.
In the BCO body frame, B=(0,0), C=(BC,0), H=(-BH,0), and O=(-BH, wheel_side*OH).
The local BCO +x axis points from B to C; local +y is the left normal of B->C. wheel_side=-1 places O on the established CAD side of the carrier.
Robot-frame angles are directed angles measured from +Ox; counter-clockwise is positive.
The directed vector D->A has angle -30 degrees in the robot frame, so D is higher than A.
The opposite directed vector A->D therefore has angle +150 degrees in the robot frame.
The four-bar solver uses a local solver frame with A=(0,0) and A->D aligned with +x; solver outputs are rotated by the derived A->D angle when transformed into the robot frame.
The physical four-bar assembly branch is -1, verified against the supplied CAD reference.
